overview: The volforecast package is an ML realized volatility forecasting system: it progressively enriches HAR-family baselines with microstructure, options-implied, and cross-asset features, mostly via gradient boosting, aiming for statistically significant QLIKE improvements and a tradeable IV-RV gap signal. This area covers its command surface. Everything funnels through one primary command, vol run --config <yaml>, which always takes the tournament code path: load an ExperimentConfig from YAML, ingest any universe symbols whose RV cache parquet is missing (skippable with --skip-ingest, and a config with mode: ingest exits after ingestion alone), then run every configured model through the tournament. The tournament trains models over rolling CV folds, optionally runs Optuna hyperparameter search that keeps the lowest-QLIKE completed trial, then computes comparison statistics (MCS bootstrap and Diebold-Mariano tests), delta-hedged straddle P&L across symbols, horizons, and models, and SHAP/ALE explainability, before writing metrics.json and an interactive Plotly dashboard and auto-updating the trial registry at workspace/research/trials.yaml. Around run sit roughly two dozen utility subcommands: eleven ingest-* fetchers for ticks, OHLCV, IV surfaces, VIX futures, GEX, cross-asset and microstructure data, plus status, audit, forecast (a live LONG/SHORT/FLAT IV-RV signal), kvar, cache tools, dashboard browsing, and three experiment-management commands. registry.py is the package hub: three dicts (models, feature layers, graph builders) filled by class decorators, imported by roughly 70 modules. Two wrappers front the CLI: the Bash ./vol script is guarded to the GS Linux Coder workspace and handles uv, venv, and nix library paths, while vol.cmd on Windows supports only the dev loop (test, lint, fmt, typecheck, exec, bg, jobs). Note for readers of this restore: config.py (ExperimentConfig), constants.py, evaluation/tournament.py, and a few registered model and feature modules are absent from disk.

modules.role: Package root. The __init__ docstring states the project thesis: enrich HAR-family baselines with microstructure, options-implied, and cross-asset features via gradient boosting to earn QLIKE improvements and tradeable IV-RV gap signals. __main__.py is the single CLI entry point: it builds an argparse tree with run as the primary command plus utility subcommands registered by per-module register() functions, then routes every run through ingest gating into the tournament. The run handler loads ExperimentConfig.from_yaml from volforecast.config, a module missing from this restore. _run_tournament wires dozens of progress callbacks (folds, boosting rounds, Optuna trials, multi-GPU HPO events, MCS stats, DH straddle, SHAP/ALE) into the Rich progress display and, after the run, updates the trial registry from metrics.json.

key_files.purpose: Package docstring stating the signal-discovery thesis and __version__ 0.2.0.
CLI entry point: builds the subcommand tree and drives the ingest-then-tournament run pipeline.
Decorator-based registries mapping string names to model, feature layer, and graph builder classes.

modules.role: One module per subcommand, each exposing register(subparsers) so __main__ can assemble the parser lazily. console.py holds the shared Rich Console singleton and logging setup used by every command. config_picker.py gives vol run an interactive terminal menu over workspace/configs/ YAMLs, newest first, ticking configs already completed per trials.yaml. status.py summarizes the ingestion manifest, audit.py validates every cached parquet against manifest contracts and regenerates data/manifest.json, and experiment.py provides trial listing, cloning a new config from a baseline, and side-by-side trial comparison. forecast.py is the live end product: a config-driven multi-model ensemble that predicts next-day RV, compares it to live ATM IV from TSDB, and emits LONG/SHORT/FLAT; kvar.py prints GSVIVS signal performance tables (Sharpe, drawdown, hit rate) across cached IV sources.

Interactive config picker for vol run when --config is omitted.
Data integrity audit of cached parquets against manifest contracts, regenerating data/manifest.json.
Shows the ingestion manifest: what is cached versus planned, and which universe symbols are missing.

Renders GSVIVS signal comparison tables across cached IV sources for same-day and next-day RV targets.

modules.role: Two wrapper scripts front python -m volforecast. The Bash ./vol refuses to run anywhere but Linux (the GS Coder workspace): it bootstraps a uv venv, enables system site-packages to expose GS-internal packages like pytickclient and pyslang, computes a nix LD_LIBRARY_PATH for C extensions, and upgrades gs-quant when below 1.6.0. Its help text is the best single map of the command surface, splitting Core, Data and Ingestion, Experiment Management, Presentation, and Environment tiers, and it adds agent-oriented arms: exec (captured output with an OUTPUT_FILE sentinel), bg (fire-and-forget with an EXIT_CODE sentinel), and jobs. vol.cmd is the Windows dev-loop shim supporting only test, test-all, testlf, lint, fmt, typecheck, exec, bg, and jobs; every other arm exits 2 pointing at the Linux workspace.

key_files.purpose: Linux-only Bash wrapper: env bootstrap plus dispatch of every subcommand and the exec/bg/jobs agent protocol.
Windows shim limited to the test/lint/typecheck dev loop with the same OUTPUT_FILE and EXIT_CODE sentinel protocol.

modules.role: Declares the volforecast distribution (version 0.2.0, Python 3.10 to 3.12) and the volforecast console script pointing at __main__:main. Core dependencies are the scientific stack plus rich, plotly, and simple-term-menu; the actual ML models live behind optional extras: ml (lightgbm, xgboost, optuna, shap), gpu (adds torch), graph (torch plus torch-geometric), and gs (gs-quant-internal, the GS data access layer). Pytest config defines unit, slow, integration, and formula markers; ./vol test skips slow tests while ./vol test-all runs everything.

key_files.purpose: Package metadata, console script, optional extras (gs, ml, gpu, graph), and pytest marker taxonomy.

glossary.definition: The loss function this project optimizes and reports for volatility forecasts; the package targets statistically significant QLIKE improvements over HAR baselines, and hyperparameter search keeps the lowest-QLIKE trial.

Heterogeneous autoregressive model family, the classical realized-volatility baseline built from daily, weekly, and monthly RV components; registered as har_family models and used as the reference the ML models must beat.
The spread between options-implied volatility and forecast realized volatility; when the forecast says IV is rich or cheap, the live signal trades it as LONG, SHORT, or FLAT.

The single code path every vol run takes: all configured models train on the same folds and are compared with statistical tests, straddle P&L, and a shared dashboard, whether there is one model or many.
Model Confidence Set procedure computed after training: a bootstrap test that identifies the subset of models statistically indistinguishable from the best, per horizon.
Diebold-Mariano test of equal predictive accuracy between two forecast series, computed in the tournament statistics stage alongside the MCS bootstrap.
Delta-hedged straddle profit and loss computed per symbol, horizon, and model; it converts forecast accuracy into an economic measure of trading value.
At-the-money implied volatility; the live forecast fetches the current 1-month ATM IV from the TSDB edrvol namespace (field 1matms) to compare against the RV forecast.
The project's IV-versus-RV trading signal family; vol kvar compares its backtest results (Sharpe, drawdown, hit rate) across the different cached IV sources.
The YAML-loaded configuration object that defines a run (universe, models, horizons, CV, tuning, tournament options); imported from volforecast.config, which is missing from this restore.
workspace/research/trials.yaml, the append-style ledger of experiments with per-horizon QLIKE numbers; vol experiments lists it, and completed runs update it automatically from metrics.json.
